c.tagline: Pakistan's calm, green planned capital beneath the Margalla Hills.

taxi.fareNote: Uber pulled out of Pakistan in 2022, so most visitors use Careem, InDrive or Yango. Traditional cabs are unmetered - agree the fare before setting off.

emergency.note: 1122 is the nationwide Rescue emergency service (ambulance, fire, rescue); 15 reaches the police.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Steer clear of political demonstrations around the Red Zone/D-Chowk, which can trigger sudden road closures and containers blocking the city.

hood_desc: A prime, central sector at the foot of the Margalla Hills, home to the trendy Kohsar Market cafes, embassies and quiet tree-lined streets; a comfortable, walkable base close to everything.
One of Islamabad's most sought-after sectors, built around the buzzing Jinnah Super Market (F-7 Markaz) with restaurants, shops and easy access to the Daman-e-Koh and Monal viewpoints above.
The city's linear central business district along Jinnah Avenue, lined with offices, banks, hotels and eateries and anchored by the Centaurus Mall; handy and well-connected by the Metrobus.
A calm, upscale residential sector with the F-8 Markaz, courts and parks; quieter than the F-6/F-7 strip and popular with families and longer-stay visitors.
One of the oldest parts of the planned city around Aabpara and Melody markets, with bustling bazaars, street food and the Lok Virsa heritage museum nearby; a lively, local, budget-friendly area.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not reliably potable.

transit.hours: The Metrobus runs roughly 06:00-22:00; local wagons and ride-hailing apps fill in earlier and later.
transit.note: Islamabad's backbone is the Metrobus bus rapid transit - the Red Line links the city with Rawalpindi via the Blue Area, and the Orange Line runs out to the international airport. Beyond the corridors, most travel is by taxi or ride-hailing app; there is no metro or tram.
transit.pay: Metrobus fares are paid with a rechargeable smart token/card bought at stations (about Rs 30-50 a ride); wagons and taxis are cash only.

bus: Daewoo Express & Faisal Movers intercity coaches

transit.m: Metrobus Orange Line toward the city (Peshawar Morr interchange, ~45 min)
Airport taxi or Careem to the F-sectors (30-45 min)

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants; small tips (chai-pani) are appreciated for service.

places.name: Melody Food Park

food.name: Karahi

places.name: Monal Restaurant

places.name: Khyber Dodai

places.name: Kabul Restaurant
places.note: Afghan rice dishes cooked in the traditional deg.

places.name: Melody Food Park

places.name: Aabpara Market

food.desc: Pink, gently salted tea whipped with milk and topped with pistachio and almond - the winter drink of the Pothohar plateau.

places.name: Melody Food Park
places.note: Pink chai poured all evening from big steel urns.

places.name: Jinnah Super Market

places.name: Khyber Dodai

food.desc: Churned yoghurt lassi, sweet or salted, and cane juice pressed at the stall with lemon and black salt. Pakistan is dry, so these are the local pours.

landmarks: Faisal Mosque
One of the world's largest mosques, its tent-like white marble form against the Margalla Hills is modern Pakistan's defining architectural image.
Pakistan Monument
A blossoming granite flower on Shakarparian hill whose four petals represent the provinces, glowing dramatically when floodlit at night.
Daman-e-Koh
The classic Margalla Hills viewpoint, where terraces overlook Islamabad's grid of green avenues and the gleaming Faisal Mosque below.
Margalla Hills National Park
A forested wilderness on the capital's doorstep, laced with hiking trails where leopards roam and Trail 3 tests weekend climbers.
Lok Virsa Museum
Pakistan's finest folk heritage museum, a colorful celebration of embroidery, truck art, music and craft traditions from every province.
Saidpur Village
A centuries-old Margalla foothill village reinvented as a heritage quarter of temples, craft shops and popular terrace restaurants.
Rawal Lake and Lake View Park
The capital's reservoir playground, offering boating, birdwatching and picnic gardens with the Margalla Hills mirrored in calm water.
Shakarparian Park
A landscaped hilltop park of gardens and monuments where visiting heads of state plant trees and locals savor skyline views.
Shah Allah Ditta Caves
Ancient caves and a 700-year-old village on the Margalla fringe, linked to Buddhist monks and centuries of travelers on the old Kabul route.
Golra Sharif Railway Museum
A working 1882 junction station turned heritage museum, its original waiting rooms packed with vintage locomotives, royal carriages and telegraph relics from the subcontinent's rail history.

train.note: There is no station in Islamabad itself; trains use Rawalpindi Railway Station (~15 km). Pakistan Railways services such as the Green Line, Tezgam and Khyber Mail run to Lahore (~5-6 hr), Karachi and Peshawar.

bus.note: Daewoo Express and Faisal Movers run frequent air-conditioned coaches from the Pir Wadhai and Faizabad terminals to Lahore (~4-5 hr on the motorway), Peshawar, Multan and Karachi; the Metrobus links Islamabad with Rawalpindi.

ferry.note: Islamabad sits on the Potohar plateau roughly 1,100 km from the Arabian Sea with no navigable river, so there are no passenger ferries; the boats on nearby Rawal and Khanpur lakes are recreational only. Pakistan has no scheduled international passenger shipping either - the old Karachi-Gulf sailings ended decades ago - so arriving or leaving by sea is not an option anywhere in the country.

half.name: Rawalpindi
half.blurb: Islamabad's bustling twin city, minutes away, with the chaotic Raja Bazaar and Saddar markets.

half.name: Taxila
half.blurb: UNESCO-listed Gandharan archaeological sites and museum about an hour northwest.

half.name: Murree
half.blurb: Colonial-era hill station in the Pir Panjal range ~1.5 hours away, cool and pine-clad, with its old Mall Road.

full.name: Nathia Gali
full.blurb: Forested Galyat hill resort at ~2,500 m, about 2.5 hours northeast, with cool-season walks and Himalayan views.

full.name: Khanpur Dam
full.blurb: Turquoise reservoir ~1 hour out, popular for boating, cliff jumping and kayaking.
